title: Robin: the right card can be in any place
wrong: On How many and One more the right card is the third of four about 95% of the time, so a child can pass steps by tapping the third card.
done: The right card is first, second, third or fourth about equally often, and One more does not always have a 1 card.
why: Guessing a place must not pass a step; the maths has to be the move.

title: Robin: count the berries before you answer
wrong: On How many a child can tap a card without touching a berry, the why picture is not their own count, and the question is not written.
done: Cards stay grey until every berry is touched (or Count with me), a wrong card shows the child's own numbered berries, and the question is written.
why: Counting is the skill being learned, so it must be needed to answer.

title: Swamp Hen: always draw the first row and column
wrong: Under the mat and at help level 2 the garden is a bare rectangle, so rows times shoots in a row cannot be seen.
done: Every garden at level 2 and up, and under the mat, shows at least its first row and first column of reeds; only the inside fades.
why: The array picture is the model for multiplication; help should fade the inside, not remove the model.

title: Swamp Hen: deal the shares and answer a turn question
wrong: Share shows a pile and empty lanes and the child does nothing; turn cannot be answered wrongly.
done: The child deals reeds into lanes by tapping and the game checks fair shares; a turn go asks which garden it becomes and can be wrong.
why: Division as fair sharing and turning arrays are ideas a child must do, not watch.
